formulas.title: Sayyid al-Istighfar
formulas.ar: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَىٰ عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ، وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي، فَاغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
formulas.tr: Allahumma anta Rabbi, la ilaha illa ant. Khalaqtani wa ana ‘abduk, wa ana ‘ala ‘ahdika wa wa‘dika mastata‘t. A‘udhu bika min sharri ma sana‘t. Abu’u laka bi-ni‘matika ‘alayya, wa abu’u laka bi-dhanbi, faghfir li, fa-innahu la yaghfirudh-dhunuba illa ant.
formulas.en: O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I hold to my covenant and promise to You as far as I am able. I seek Your protection from the harm of what I have done. I admit Your favours upon me and I admit my sin, so forgive me — for none forgives sins except You.
formulas.note: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever says it during the day with firm faith and dies before evening is among the people of Paradise — and the same for the night.

formulas.title: Astaghfirullah wa atubu ilayh
formulas.en: I ask Allah for forgiveness and I turn back to Him in repentance.
formulas.note: The Prophet ﷺ said that he sought Allah's forgiveness and turned to Him in repentance more than seventy times a day.

formulas.title: Rabbighfir li wa tub ‘alayya
formulas.ar: رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَتُبْ عَلَيَّ، إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ
formulas.tr: Rabbighfir li wa tub ‘alayya, innaka antat-Tawwabur-Rahim.
formulas.en: My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance. Truly You are the One who keeps accepting repentance, the Most Merciful.
formulas.note: Ibn ‘Umar reported that the Companions would count the Prophet ﷺ saying this a hundred times in a single gathering.

formulas.title: Astaghfirullah al-‘Azim…
formulas.ar: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ الْعَظِيمَ الَّذِي لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيَّ الْقَيُّومَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ
formulas.tr: Astaghfirullahal-‘Azim alladhi la ilaha illa huwal-Hayyul-Qayyumu wa atubu ilayh.
formulas.en: I ask forgiveness of Allah, the Supreme — there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all — and I turn to Him in repentance.
formulas.note: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever says this will be forgiven, even if he had fled from the battlefield.

formulas.title: Astaghfirullah
formulas.note: When the Prophet ﷺ finished his prayer he would say “Astaghfirullah” three times.

benefits.head: Rain, wealth, children and gardens
benefits.intro: Prophet Nuh (Noah) told his people what istighfar opens up:

benefits.head: A good life until the appointed time
benefits.intro: Allah promises those who seek pardon and turn back to Him:

promise.head: The promise of Nuh ﷺ: rain, wealth, children, gardens and rivers
promise.note: Allah links seeking forgiveness directly to rain, wealth, children, gardens and rivers — five kinds of provision in three ayat.

promise.head: A good life — “good sustenance until a stated term”
promise.note: Istighfar and returning to Allah (tawbah) together: sustenance in this life and grace in the next.

promise.head: Hud ﷺ: rain and “strength added to your strength”
promise.note: Ibn Kathir: this covers strength in wealth, children and power.

promise.head: A shield from punishment
promise.note: As long as people keep seeking forgiveness, Allah does not punish them.

promise.head: Provision from where you never expected
promise.note: Promised to whoever has taqwa (mindfulness of Allah) and trusts Him — istighfar is the door back to taqwa.

salaf.text: Four men came to him: one complained of drought, one of poverty, one of having no children, one that his garden was dry. He told each of them: “Seek Allah’s forgiveness.” When asked why he gave one answer to four problems, he recited Nuh 71:10–12.
salaf.src: Reported by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir of Surah Nuh

salaf.text: He went out to pray for rain and did nothing but seek forgiveness until he returned. Asked why, he said: “I sought rain through the keys of the sky,” and recited 71:10–11.
salaf.src: Reported by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir of Surah Nuh

conditions: Istighfar while insisting on a sin is weak. Leave it now — or start leaving it.
Genuine remorse in the heart. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Regret is repentance” (Ibn Majah 4252, sahih).
Sincerely intend not to go back, even if you slip later — then repent again.
If the sin involved someone else — money, honour, a debt — return it or seek their pardon.
Your heart should mean what your tongue says. Slow down, understand the words.

plan.why: “Whoever says it during the day with firm faith and dies that day before evening is among the people of Jannah” (Bukhari 6306).
The Prophet ﷺ — who was already forgiven — sought forgiveness 100 times a day (Muslim 2702) and more than 70 times (Bukhari 6307).
Ibn Umar counted the Prophet ﷺ saying it 100 times in one sitting (Abu Dawud 1516, Tirmidhi 3434 — sahih).

plan.what: “Astaghfirullāh al-ʿAẓīm alladhī lā ilāha illā Huwa…”
plan.why: Whoever says it is forgiven, even if he fled from battle (Tirmidhi 3577, Abu Dawud 1517 — sahih).

plan.time: Last third of the night (before Fajr)
plan.why: Allah praises “those who seek forgiveness before dawn” (3:17, 51:18). Allah descends and asks: “Who seeks My forgiveness, that I may forgive him?” (Bukhari 1145).
“…and whoever says it at night with firm faith and dies before morning is among the people of Jannah” (Bukhari 6306).

tahajjud: The last third of the night is best. Example: Maghrib 6:00 pm, Fajr 5:00 am → the night is 11 h, so the last third starts around 1:20 am. Any time after Isha counts.
Pray two rakʿat at a time, as many as you can, then finish with an odd number (Witr) — the Prophet ﷺ taught this (Bukhari 472). Even 2 rakʿat + 1 Witr is tahajjud.

Allah descends to the nearest heaven in the last third and says: “Who is calling Me, that I may answer? Who is asking Me, that I may give? Who seeks My forgiveness, that I may forgive?” (Bukhari 1145, Muslim 758).
“The best prayer after the obligatory prayers is the night prayer” (Muslim 1163).
After your rakʿat, sit and seek forgiveness until Fajr — this is exactly who Allah praises in 3:17 and 51:18. Then make du‘a for your provision, debts and family.
Sleep early, make wudu before bed, set an alarm 20 minutes before Fajr. If you miss it, the Prophet ﷺ made it up in the day (Muslim 746).
gem.honesty: A popular narration — “Whoever persists in istighfar, Allah will give him a way out of every distress and provide for him from where he does not expect” (Abu Dawud 1518, Ibn Majah 3819) — is graded weak (daʿīf) by al-Albani and Shuʿayb al-Arnaʾūṭ. Shukr only presents it with this label. Its meaning is supported by the Qur’an itself (11:3, 65:2–3, 71:10–12). Istighfar is worship, not a transaction: Allah gives provision as He wills — wealth, peace, barakah, or something better saved for you. Keep working hard and earning halal; istighfar opens the doors.
hadith: “Glad tidings to whoever finds in their record of deeds a lot of istighfar.”
“O son of Adam, if your sins reached the clouds of the sky and then you asked My forgiveness, I would forgive you.”
“By Allah, I seek Allah’s forgiveness and repent to Him more than seventy times a day.”
“Sometimes a cloud covers my heart, and I seek Allah’s forgiveness a hundred times a day.”
